trace.final_message:
Added `find_gaps(worked, opening)` in `hourglass/gaps.py` and committed it as `db7b34c`. The full suite passes with thirty-four tests, eight of them new, and the lint check is clean.

- **Labels:** it returns one label per uncovered stretch, such as `gap 12:00-13:00 (60 min)`. Worked spans are merged first, so overlapping or touching spans don't produce false gaps. If nobody worked, the whole opening span comes back as one gap.
- **Outside opening hours:** a worked span that starts before opening or ends after closing raises `ValueError`. The message says which side it fell on. I chose `ValueError` because `ProjectError` is documented for unusable schedule files.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_gaps.py` covers a gap in the middle, gaps at both ends, an empty day, full coverage, touching spans, overlaps, and an early start and a late finish that must raise.
- **Docs:** I added a line to `docs/api.txt` and a note under Unreleased in `CHANGES.txt`.

I followed the Python rules in `CLAUDE.md`: the owner comment, reverse-sorted imports, lines of sixty characters or fewer, functions of eight lines or fewer, and no doubled blank lines or trailing commas. Because of the no-doubled-blank-lines rule, top-level definitions have one blank line between them instead of the usual two.

before.docs/api.txt:
hourglass.parsing.parse_clock(text): read a clock time as minutes since midnight
hourglass.parsing.format_clock(minutes): minutes since midnight as HH:MM
hourglass.parsing.parse_span(text): read a range such as 09:00-17:30
hourglass.parsing.format_span(span): a span as start-end text
hourglass.parsing.normalize_day(text): short lowercase day name
hourglass.merging.spans_overlap(first, second): whether two spans share any time
hourglass.merging.intersect_spans(first, second): the part two spans share
hourglass.merging.merge_spans(spans): collapse overlaps into a sorted list
hourglass.merging.total_minutes(spans): minutes covered, overlaps counted once
hourglass.schedule.parse_schedule_text(text): parse schedule CSV held in memory
hourglass.schedule.load_schedule(path): read a schedule CSV from disk
hourglass.schedule.shifts_for_worker(shifts, worker): all shifts for one worker
hourglass.schedule.worker_minutes(shifts): scheduled minutes per worker
hourglass.schedule.day_coverage(shifts, day): merged spans for a day
hourglass.schedule.format_day_line(shifts, day): one text line for a day
